description: A polyphonic oscillator built by adding sixteen sine waves, each with its own frequency multiple, level and phase

params.text: Sets how much of this sine wave goes into the sum, -1 to 1, starting at 0; a negative setting turns that sine upside down
Shifts where in its cycle this sine wave starts, 0 to 0.999 of a cycle
Multiplies the base frequency for this sine wave, a whole number from 0 to 32, starting at this block's own number counting left to right and top to bottom
Sets the base frequency the oscillator plays at 0V, 10Hz to 20000Hz, starting at 261.626Hz for C4; the scale is linear in Hz, so most of the travel covers the top of the range
Multiplies the sum of all sixteen sine waves, 0 to 1, starting at 0.5

inputs.text: Sets this sine wave's level directly over -10V to 10V for -1 to 1, overriding its Level knob while patched
Added to this sine wave's phase knob at a tenth of a cycle per volt, with the sign of the voltage thrown away so a negative voltage shifts the same way as a positive one
Multiplies the base frequency by its own voltage divided by ten, so 10V doubles it and -10V takes it to nothing; the result is held between 10Hz and 20000Hz
Sets the pitch at 1V per octave from the base frequency knob's setting at 0V, and sets how many polyphonic voices the module plays

outputs.text: Carries the sum of the sixteen sine waves after the output level knob, at the same number of polyphonic channels as the pitch input

notes: every Level knob starts at 0, so a freshly placed module is silent until at least one of them is raised
the sum is not limited in any way; sixteen sines at full level reach far past ±10V, so keep the output level knob down and put a limiter after this module
with nothing patched to V-In the oscillator plays one voice at the base frequency knob's setting
a Mult knob at 0 does not silence its sine wave but freezes it at one point of the cycle, adding a fixed voltage to the output; the maker's manual says 0 does not add to the signal
the level jacks replace their knobs while patched rather than adding to them, and the phase jacks add to theirs
the Pitch In jack works two ways: with V-In empty it scales the knob's frequency, and with V-In patched it adds a fixed number of hertz taken from the knob, not from the note played
the sixteen level jacks are labelled 0 to 10V in Rack's tooltips, but they read -10V to 10V as the manual says
